correctness.rationale: For any d>=2 and p>2, recenter A,B at a,b. Their support functions and g(u)=h_{Q(A-a)}(u)-h_{B-b}(u) are even. Residual translation z=Qa+t-b contributes the odd term z·u. Antipodal pairing writes the pth-power objective as integral of (|g+z·u|^p+|g-z·u|^p)/2. Strict convexity of |.|^p makes this >=|g|^p, with strict inequality wherever z·u≠0. For z≠0 the equatorial zero set has sphere measure zero; hence the unique minimum for each fixed Q is z=0 and every globally optimal rigid motion aligns symmetry centers. Does NOT imply unique Q, and p=2 is not claimed new.

evidence: Herburt–Moszyńska 2009 proves existence of Lp-optimal rigid isometries and recalls Arnold p=2 Steiner-point alignment.
The indexed all-body p>2 nonexistence concerns the unrestricted convex-body class; it does not forbid a selector on the symmetric subclass.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither existence nor the p=2 result implies center alignment for finite p>2 as stated; the full-class impossibility has a different universal quantifier.

originality.rationale: The source 2009 paper defines the Lp support-function metric and optimal isometries and discusses the Steiner point for p=2, but its existence theorem is not a center-alignment theorem for arbitrary finite p>2 restricted to centrally symmetric bodies. A Resultary-indexed negative result for a selector on the full class is compatible: it does not disprove restricted center alignment. Best-of-knowledge novelty is the restricted selector property and per-orientation uniqueness, not the classical strict-convexity inequality.
residual_risks: A concise parity/Jensen argument could have appeared as an uncatalogued remark in approximation geometry.
The all-body p>2 negative selector problem remains unsolved by this restricted affirmative result; no uniqueness of optimal orientation is proved.
